$comment: What x.com's composer runs to count a post, fingerprinted. tools/build-core.mjs builds src/core.js from twitter-text 3.1.0 and @twemoji/parser 15.0.0, applies the edits below, and refuses to write the core unless every pattern it produces has the SHA-256 recorded here. Each hash is of the pattern's source text as the composer compiles it.
where: https://x.com/compose/post, signed in, in a desktop browser
how: The composer's own counting functions (parseTweet and extractUrls in the bundle) were called in the page on the 1,731,072 strings test/reference/corpus.js generates, and the digests of their answers are recorded below. test/reference/x-live-reference.js rebuilds the same answers from the published packages and the four differences listed here. The patterns those functions use were captured while they ran and hashed.
digestFormat: For each run of 50,000 strings, the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of their answer lines joined together. A line is `${weightedLength},${valid ? 1 : 0},${validRangeEnd}|${links}` and a newline, from the composer's parseTweet(s), with links from its extractUrls(s.normalize()) as `${start}:${end}:${url.length}` joined by commas.
differences: Seven domain endings that twitter-text 3.1.0 does not have, each placed where the composer's list has it: amazon, kids, music, spa, アマゾン and 亚马逊 (generic), ישראל (country).
U+FEFF is no longer one of the invalid characters, so it may stand before a link and inside a domain.
A bare domain ending in .md is not a link. With a protocol it still is.
The emoji pattern is @twemoji/parser 15.0.0's, with U+1FAF0 moved from the group that takes U+FE0F into the group that takes only a skin tone.
differencesAreComplete: With these four changes switched off and twitter-text 3.1.0 run in Node with twemoji-parser 14.0.0, test/reference/x-live-reference.js gives the same answer as twitter-text on every one of the 1,731,072 strings; with them on, it gives x.com's digests. So these four are the whole difference on that corpus.
alsoCorrected: Not a difference in x.com: punycode measures U+0000-U+001F and U+007F in a domain label as ASCII, as x.com's bundled punycode and Node's built-in one do. The first version of this package encoded them, as the npm punycode twitter-text declares (1.4.1) does.
